prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (≤500 words)

Scope and goal:
- UK-wide programme centred on a 10‑year Green New Deal to reach net-zero emissions by 2030, paired with measures on democracy, public services, taxation, and social policy.

Green New Deal (investment of £100+bn/year plus UBI):
- Energy: Rapid expansion of wind (target ~70% of electricity by 2030), plus solar, tidal, hydro and geothermal; remove fossil fuel subsidies; rising carbon tax on domestic and imported fossil fuels/embedded emissions; stronger interconnectors; double grid capacity; expand storage; ban fracking; prohibit new nuclear.
- Housing: Insulate every home by 2030; deep retrofit 1m homes/year (10m by 2030); rooftop renewables for 1m homes/year; replace gas boilers with heat pumps/renewable heat; heat networks; 100,000 new social homes/year to Passivhaus standard; rental stock to EPC A by 2030; planning and building regs strengthened.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; £2.5bn/year for cycling/walking; reopen lines, electrify rail, shift freight to rail; local control of buses and tram schemes; public ownership of rail over 10 years; end sale of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; nationwide EV charging; frequent flyer levy; halt new runways and road capacity; 20mph default in residential areas; cancel HS2 and redirect funds.
- Industry/circular economy: Grants/R&D to decarbonise process heat and machinery; regional mutual banks; just transition for North Sea/coal; £2bn/year for skills; right‑to‑repair and 10‑year warranties; phase out single-use plastics; extended producer responsibility; CCS for steel/cement; strict efficiency standards.
- Food, farming & forestry: 10‑year shift to agroecology; 700m trees; half of farms in agroforestry by 2030; major pesticide reductions; hedgerow restoration; urban growing; right to food; nature‑based flood management; restrict building on floodplains; consider meat/dairy levy phased in over 10 years with revenues recycled to support farm transition.

Incomes and welfare:
- Phase in Universal Basic Income: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; child supplements (higher for incomes under £50k); supplements for disabled and lone parents; retain housing benefit; funded partly by carbon tax.

Democracy and governance:
- Proportional representation; votes at 16; elected second chamber; state funding of parties; stronger lobbying and transparency rules; digital rights; citizens’ assemblies and a written constitution; new climate‑focused finance post (annual carbon budgets); Future Generations Act; restructure departments for sanctuary and peace; end arms export promotion; expand devolution and powers/funding for councils (+£10bn/year; £3bn climate adaptation; free home care for over‑65s).

International/EU:
- Public vote on any Brexit deal with a remain option; EU reforms for transparency, citizen law‑initiation, social and environmental standards; humane refugee policy; EU‑wide carbon border adjustment; aid increased to 1% of GNI; debt relief; ecocide law; high‑standard trade without ISDS.

Public services:
- NHS: +£6bn/year to 2030; reverse marketisation; community health centres; timely mental health access; free contraception; PrEP provision.
- Education: +£4bn/year; reduce testing/replace Ofsted; formal schooling from 6; return schools to local control; inclusive SEND; climate/nature curriculum and new Nature GCSE; scrap tuition fees and write off £9k‑era debt; expand FE/adult learning.

Justice, drugs, rights, animals:
- Halve prison population via fewer short sentences and restorative justice; invest in youth services and community policing.
- Replace prohibition with regulated drug markets; expunge past possession/small‑scale supply convictions; heroin‑assisted treatment; safe consumption rooms; legal regulated cannabis.
- Strategies against discrimination; humane immigration with an end to indefinite detention; misogyny as hate crime; expand support for survivors; LGBTIQA+ and disability rights strengthened.
- Recognise animal sentience; ban hunting/snaring; end badger cull; tighten animal transport; phase out factory farming practices; stronger regulation and oversight.

Tax, spending, and funding:
- Consolidate income-related taxes to tax income from wealth like work; replace personal allowance with UBI; Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax/Business Rates over 10 years with protections; Corporation Tax to 24%; bank taxes; independent HMRC; anti‑avoidance measures; clamp down on tax havens and non‑dom status.
- Small business support: regional mutual banks; credit guidance; 15% of public contracts to small firms; tackle late payments; raise Employment Allowance; VAT cuts for hospitality/culture; promote co‑ops; nationwide high‑speed broadband.
- Cancel Trident renewal, major road building, airport expansion, HS2, Help to Buy; end NHS internal market.
- Fiscal plan: ~£141.5bn/year operational spend funded by tax changes and savings; ~£94.4bn/year capital via borrowing; expected £76.7bn/year carbon tax revenue; anticipated private co‑investment ~£50bn/year.
